issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-14759](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-14759)
### Description

The postgres_fdw extension largely works out of the box because YugabyteDB speaks the same wire protocol as postgres. This also implies that a foreign server can be either:
 - Another YugabyteDB instance (or even the same one via loopback)
 - A vanilla Postgres instance

Most queries should work on both types of foreign servers; however there are specific differences in the wire protocol used by both:
 - System columns: When `use_remote_estimate` is used to procure row estimates from the foreign server, postgres_fdw sends `SELECT ctid FROM <foreign table>` query to the foreign server to get row estimates at planning time. YugabyteDB does not use the system column ctid, and instead uses ybctids (#11419).

I situations, such as the ones listed above, it would be useful to know what type of a foreign server the postgres_fdw is interacting with. There are a few ways to implement this:
 - At the time of creating the foreign server, have the user pass in a "server_type" attribute as an option.
 - Parse the output of `SELECT version()`
 - Use the presence of YugabyteDB specific objects and functions to determine the type of foreign server.
